title: The Strategy Process
coreMove: Cross-examine a strategy until the how, capability, milestones, and economics are visible.
sourcePressure: Core process two: strategy has to explain the hows and test external environment, customers, markets, competition, executable capability, milestones, time balance, critical issues, and sustainable economics. No chapter-specific named company case is frozen.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treat strategy as a polished destination statement or framework exercise.

hook: the the strategy process that nobody sees until it is too late
a meeting room where every plan sounds good
a generic promise colliding with reality
counterintuition: Most leaders think X, but the opposite is true
The problem is not effort, it is discipline
Execution is not about working harder
tryThisNow: set a timer and write three priorities
audit one goal in your notebook
ask yourself what matters most today
examples: generic project kickoff with vague owners
student team with a deadline and no specificity
family calendar scene used as a management analogy

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional grocery co-op planning online pickup in towns where customers still shop by weekly flyer
exampleSpecs.audience: a general manager building a growth plan
exampleSpecs.stakes: the co-op can spend on software before proving customer behavior and profitable route density
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie refuses to approve the pickup strategy until the plan answers customers, competition, route economics, capability, and milestones
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Who is the strategy for if the weekly flyer still decides Thursday shopping?

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional soccer academy expanding into winter futsal while rival clubs own the gym slots
exampleSpecs.stakes: growth stalls if competition and capacity are not part of the plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Daniel turns a growth slogan into a strategic plan by writing the rival gym slots and coach availability beside the target
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The indoor gym schedule is already full of rival club names when Daniel opens the expansion plan.

exampleSpecs.domain: a medical publisher deciding whether to launch a continuing-education subscription
exampleSpecs.stakes: the subscription can attract users but fail sustainable economics after accreditation costs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Antoine asks how the offer makes money on a sustainable basis before the launch team celebrates subscriber interest
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 2:34 p.m., Antoine sees a strong survey result beside an accreditation invoice estimate.

exampleSpecs.domain: a coastal ferry authority balancing short-term schedule fixes against long-term vessel replacement
exampleSpecs.stakes: passenger reliability can improve briefly while the capital issue worsens
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Henrik forces the plan to name the short-term and long-term balance instead of hiding replacement risk under service tweaks
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Show me where the old hull appears in this plan," Henrik says, tapping the timetable.

exampleSpecs.domain: a small cosmetics manufacturer entering pharmacies while its batch testing lab is already at capacity
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder choosing a channel strategy
exampleSpecs.stakes: new accounts can outstrip testing capability and damage retailer trust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Paula traces a failed pharmacy pitch to a strategy that never asked whether the business could execute the channel shift
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Paula one returned pharmacy contract to notice the batch-testing queue buried in the appendix.

exampleSpecs.domain: a nonprofit refugee-services agency adding job-placement programs without employer partnerships
exampleSpecs.stakes: clients can be promised outcomes the agency has no partner network to deliver
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chidi rewrites the strategic plan around employer partnerships, milestones, and capability instead of mission language alone
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You read the mission paragraph and Chidi reads the empty employer-partnership list underneath it.

skillTargets: test whether a strategy names the hows
identify missing customer, competition, capability, and economics questions
choose milestones that prove progress instead of decorate it

tryThisNowSpec: Take one strategy sentence and add the missing how: customer, competition, capability, milestone, or sustainable economics.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
